deities: Goddess Mahalakshmi (kuladevi of the Agrawal community)

history.period: Modern: construction 1976 - 1984; legendary capital from Dwapara Yuga (traditional)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: Agroha Dham is NOT in Hisar city - it is in the town of Agroha, Hisar district, Haryana 125047, about 20 km from Hisar city. Documented with the corrected town. Agroha Dham is the principal temple complex of the Agrawal community, dedicated to Goddess Mahalakshmi (their kuladevi) and the legendary king Maharaja Agrasen. Tradition holds Agroha was Agrasen's capital in the Dwapara Yuga; the adjacent Agroha Mound (ASI-protected since 1926) shows a fortified township inhabited from the 4th century BCE to the 14th century CE, on the ancient Taxila-Mathura trade route, destroyed by Muhammad of Ghor in 1194. The site was revived in 1907-08 when ascetic Brahmananda Brahmachari organized the Agrawal Darbar. The modern complex was decided at the 1976 All India Agarwal Representatives convention; the Agroha Vikas Trust (Shri Krishna Modi, Rameshwar Das Gupta) was formed, land was donated by Laxmi Narayan Gupta, construction began under Tilak Raj Aggarwal and the main temple was completed in 1984, with later works (including the Shakti Sarovar, filled in 1988 with water from 41 holy rivers of India) under Subhash Goel from 1985. The complex follows a triangular Nagara-style layout with three wings: Mahalakshmi (center), Agrasen (east), Saraswati (west).

name: Agroha Dham
town_description: Agroha is a historic town in Hisar district, Haryana, held by tradition to be the capital of the legendary king Maharaja Agrasen and the origin-place of the Agrawal community; its archaeological mound shows continuous habitation from the 4th century BCE to the 14th century CE.

travel.airport: Hisar Airport (~15 km); Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~170 km) for better connectivity
travel.railway: Hisar Junction (nearest major railhead); the temple is a ~30-minute drive from the station via NH 52
travel.road: On National Highway 52 (NH 52); regular buses and taxis from Hisar city

visitor_information.best_time: October - March; the Agroha Maha Kumbh on Sharad Purnima (October) is the grandest annual event
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM - 8:30 PM; morning aarti 8:00 AM, evening aarti 7:00 PM (2026 schedule per Bharat Temples)
